data.summary: The final answer is the content of the last complete <ascii_formatted>...</ascii_formatted> block in the final message, taken from the last opening tag before the last closing tag. That content is normalized by stripping it, unifying newlines, rstripping each line, and dropping blank lines and stray ``` fence lines. The gold is normalized the same way. If the tag is missing or the line lists differ in any way, the reward is 0.0; otherwise the original reward is returned unchanged. This exact-match rule stops credit for trees that are missing a line, have one line changed, or append a second tree, since the original graders only gave partial credit by line. Correct answers still pass when they include reasoning or <think> text before the tags, or carry trailing whitespace or fences.

Extract <ascii_formatted> content the same way the original XMLParser does: a non-greedy match from the opening tag to the next closing tag. Both the first and last such blocks are checked, and a block that itself contains an ascii_formatted tag is rejected, which closes the nested-tag bypass. Each block is normalized exactly as the audit's verifier does: unify newlines, strip the block, split into lines and rstrip each line. Blank or whitespace-only lines and fence-like lines are no longer dropped. The resulting line list must equal the gold's normalized lines, otherwise the reward is 0.0. When the check passes, the original reward is returned unchanged.

Extract every <ascii_formatted>...</ascii_formatted> block from the final message; there must be at least one, and every block (first, middle and last) must contain no nested tags and, after stripping, splitting on '\n' only (as the original rewards do, so a bare carriage return is no longer turned into a line break and any remaining '\r' inside a line fails) and rstripping each line, must equal the gold tree normalized the same way. Otherwise the reward is 0.0; passing responses keep their original reward unchanged.
